packages.title: Apple CEO transition: Ternus in, Cook to chair
mirroredFacts: John Ternus becomes Apple CEO on September 1, 2026.
Tim Cook becomes Apple executive chairman on September 1, 2026.
packages.postText:
Apple’s CEO transition lands tomorrow.

John Ternus takes over as CEO on Sept. 1. Tim Cook becomes executive chairman after 15 years in the top job.

This isn’t a product-cycle headline. It’s a leadership handoff at a $4T company heading into its next AI chapter.

packages.title: Bitcoin: CK Zheng's $150K late-2027 forecast

benchmarkMapping.rank1Disposition: Previously blocked at 2026-09-01T04:41Z; not reconsidered because no primary source substantiated its central $35B claim.
benchmarkMapping.rank2Disposition: Skipped: Federal Reserve materials confirm the meeting but do not substantiate the claimed 55% probability or an outcome before the meeting.

mirroredFacts: CK Zheng is the former global head of valuation risk at Credit Suisse and co-founder/CIO of ZX Squared Capital.
Zheng told Investing.com that he expects Bitcoin to reach $150,000 by late 2027.
The forecast was presented as Zheng's opinion and cited institutional adoption and regulatory clarity as part of his rationale.

materialFacts.fact: Bitcoin could reach $150,000 by late 2027, according to CK Zheng.
The claim is an attributed market forecast, not a company filing, official price target, or investment recommendation.

packages.verificationNotes: Rank 3 was verified through contemporaneous authoritative financial reporting of a direct interview. Wording keeps the price target explicitly attributed to Zheng. No benchmark text or imagery was reused.
packages.postText:
Bitcoin is staring at a $150K call for late 2027.

CK Zheng, ex-Credit Suisse risk chief, told Investing.com the worst of the cycle may be over.

The thesis: institutional adoption and clearer regulation.

A forecast—not a catalyst.

posts.title: Intel proposed stock offering
posts.text:
Intel just announced a proposed $15B common stock offering.

It also gave underwriters a 30-day option to buy up to another $2.25B.
Intel said the proceeds may be used for general corporate purposes, including CapEx and working capital.
